The GL double layered cloak consists of two spherical annular layers: inner layer R1 ≤ r ≤ R2 and outer layer R2 ≤ r ≤ R3.
The outer layer cloak provides invisibility, allowing external EM waves to propagate as in free space without disturbance.
The inner layer cloak fully absorbs EM waves excited by sources inside the concealed region, preventing their escape.
The metamaterials used are anisotropic, weakly dispersive, and weakly degenerative.
The GL method combines analytical and numerical modeling without large matrix equations or artificial boundaries.
The GL method divides the domain into subdomains and updates global fields by local interactions.
The cloak ensures no Maxwell EM wavefield can be excited by nonzero local sources inside a single-layer cloak with normal materials.
The GL double layered cloak overcomes the divergence and chaos problems of single-layer cloaks with internal sources.
Simulations used a 3D domain of 1m³ with a 201×201×201 mesh grid and 0.005 m mesh size.
The cloak's inner and outer layers have distinct anisotropic permittivity and permeability tensors tailored for absorption and invisibility.
The GL method does not require perfectly matched layer (PML) conditions to truncate infinite domains.
The cloak maintains a normal EM environment inside the concealed region, allowing Maxwell EM wavefields from internal sources.
The interface at radius R2 couples the two cloak layers ensuring continuity and functionality.
The GL EM integral equation uses Green's tensors excited by point impulse currents in the background medium.
The cloak materials' parameter variation matrix δ[D] is a diagonal or full matrix depending on anisotropy.
The GL method is meshless and supports arbitrary geometries including spherical, cylindrical, and rectangular subdomains.
The cloak's design satisfies Maxwell boundary conditions and integral equations ensuring invisibility and absorption.
The GL method reduces numerical dispersion compared to FEM and FDTD methods.
The cloak's outer layer prevents penetration of external EM waves into the inner layer and concealed region.
The inner layer absorbs internal EM waves completely, preventing any reflection or transmission outside.
